Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Server Policy → From a line profile

New Server Policy from a line

A guided build that turns a line profile and one or more web addresses into complete server policies — address, DNS record, certificate and device objects — and reports exactly what was undone and what was left behind if a step fails.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view network.edit network.apply protection.edit protection.apply
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy → From a line profile (URL /workspace/<appliance_id>/spo-wizard)

What is it?#

The wizard builds new server policies from a line. The line's profile supplies the network segment, the certificate class and the Web Protection Profile; you supply the web addresses and the real servers. One run can reserve the VIP in IPAM, publish the hostname in DNS, issue the certificate and create the objects on the FortiWeb — and if a step fails, it lists separately what it undid and what it deliberately left behind.

What does it do?#

  • Builds one server policy, virtual server, VIP, DNS record and certificate per domain, and one server pool shared by all domains of the run.
  • Derives every object name from the web address through the FortiWeb patterns saved on the Naming page (built-in defaults where no pattern is saved).
  • Checks the whole plan before anything is written, including a live check of the device for a policy or pool with the same name and for the line's Web Protection Profile, and reports every blocker at once.
  • Serves HTTPS with the certificate it issues: the new server policy is bound to it.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the wizard now uses your saved naming patterns, binds the certificate it issues to the new server policy, and blocks the plan when the line's Web Protection Profile does not exist on the device.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the Server Policy list that carries From a line profile is at FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy (FortiWeb's own menu); the Loadbalancer group is gone.

  • Lets you bind an existing pool on the device, or copy the members of a pool cached from another FortiWeb into a new pool.
  • Lets you choose the IPAM and DNS backend, or leave both on Auto.
  • Refuses the whole batch if any domain is blocked.

Requirements#

  • A selected FortiWeb (the page is reached from its Server Policy list).
  • At least one line defined, ideally with a line profile (see Line profiles and Classification). Without a profile the wizard still works but every value is inferred.
  • Network segments assigned to the line (see Segments).
  • For Reserve the VIP from IPAM: a backend with the IPAM role and a pool declared by the line profile or the segment.
  • For a published hostname: a backend with the DNS role that can write records. Both are configured in Settings → DNS Records (see Settings).
  • For Issue the certificate: a certificate class on the line, with a CA template configured in Settings → Certificate Manager.
  • A working naming scheme that produces names for the server policy, virtual server, server pool and VIP.

Permissions#

Opening the wizard needs protection.view and a device you can see.

Both Preview (writes nothing) and Apply call the same endpoint, which requires the legacy config_write permission — any of network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit, protection.apply or another key that implies it. The Operator and Administrator profiles have them.

🔑Permission — Without config_write

The form opens normally, but Preview (writes nothing) returns nothing: the result card shows nothing to show and the badge blocked.

How to use#

  1. 1Pick the lineDepartment and segment narrow the network
  2. 2Add domainsOne row per web address
  3. 3Choose the poolNew from real servers, or an existing one
  4. 4PreviewEvery blocker and warning, the exact payloads
  5. 5ApplyConfirm; runs domain by domain
  6. 6Read the resultbuilt, undone, left behind

Describe what to build#

  1. Open FortiWeb → Policy → Server Policy and press From a line profile in the page header.
  2. Choose a Line. A line without a profile is listed with (no profile), and the note under it says the values were INFERRED.
  3. Optional: choose a Department to narrow the Segment list. Choose the Segment when the line receives more than one.
  4. Under Domains to build, fill one row per domain: the web address (for example www.example.com), the port that goes into {port} in the object names (blank = the port in the address, else 443 with a certificate and 80 without), the hostname to publish (blank = do not publish), and the VIP (blank when using IPAM; typed by hand it must sit in one of the segment's networks). Use Add another domain for more rows; × removes a row (the last row is only cleared). A flow that calls the wizard's API sends port in each web_addresses entry.
  5. Tick Reserve the VIP from IPAM and/or Issue the certificate as needed.

Choose the server pool#

  • Create a new pool from these real servers (one ip:port per line) — type the real servers, for example 192.0.2.21:8080. A line without a port uses 80.
  • Use a server pool that already exists — search by pool name, device or member IP, then pick:
  • a pool marked this device is bound; no pool or member is created and the real servers above are ignored;
  • a pool marked OTHER device cannot be bound (a server pool belongs to one device). Press Copy its members and create a new pool here to copy its ip:port members into the new-pool list. Weight, SSL and health-check settings are not copied.

Choose the backends#

IPAM backend (the address) and DNS backend (the hostname) list only enabled backends with that role, each with its provider and declared scope. Auto — resolve from the declared scope follows the scopes in Settings → DNS Records. A chosen backend overrides the choice only; it never widens a scope.

Preview and apply#

  1. Press Preview (writes nothing). The Result card shows, per domain, buildable or blocked, the resolved segment, backends and pool, every blocker with its code, every warning, the steps, and Device payloads.
  2. When every domain is buildable, Apply becomes active.
  3. Press Apply and confirm the dialog that lists the domains.
  4. Read the result: the steps of each domain, built: with the domains that completed, undone: lines and left behind: lines.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Line The line whose profile supplies segment, certificate class and Web Protection Profile. Yes internet
Department Narrows the segments; never picks one on its own. No sales
Segment Network the VIP lives on. Required when the line has several. Conditional dmz-web
Web address One per domain; all object names derive from it. Yes www.example.com
Hostname DNS name to publish. Blank = not published. No www.example.com
VIP Address of the VIP when IPAM is not used. When IPAM is off 192.0.2.10
Reserve the VIP from IPAM Takes the next free address per domain. No on
Issue the certificate Issues a certificate of the line's class for the hostname (or the web address). No on
Server pool New pool from real servers, or an existing pool. Yes 192.0.2.21:8080
IPAM backend / DNS backend Auto or a specific backend. No Auto

Example#

🧪Example — Two shop domains behind one pool

Line internet, segment dmz-web, IPAM on, certificate on, real servers 192.0.2.21:8080 and 192.0.2.22:8080, domains shop.example.com and www.example.com.

Preview shows two buildable plans. The first creates the pool (created by this policy), the second binds it (created by the FIRST domain of this batch). Each plan reserves an address, publishes an A record, issues a certificate and creates a virtual server, VIP and server policy; the pool and its two members are written once.

Result#

  • Per domain, in this order: the address is reserved (or the supplied VIP is used), the DNS record is created, the certificate is issued, then the device objects are created — Virtual Server, VIP, Server Pool and Pool member N (only for a new pool), and Server Policy bound to the virtual server, the pool and the line's Web Protection Profile. When the run issued a certificate, the policy also gets the HTTPS service and that certificate.
  • One audit entry spo_wizard.apply per domain, naming device, line, department, segment, address, pool, backends, outcome and the number of leftovers.
  • On failure, compensation acts only on what this run recorded:
  • a DNS record this run created is removed;
  • an address this run reserved is released;
  • an issued certificate is not revoked — it is listed under left behind:;
  • device objects already created are listed, not deleted;
  • domains of the batch that were already built are listed as already built and NOT undone and stay in place.

❗Important

The certificate is issued and deployed by the Certificate Manager (see Certificates) and then bound to the new server policy, which serves HTTPS with it (predefined HTTPS service). Without Issue the certificate, the policy is written without a certificate; bind one on the policy's detail page if the policy serves HTTPS.

Troubleshooting#

A domain shows blocked#

Each blocker carries a code. The most common:

Code Meaning Fix
no_web_address The row has no web address. Fill it.
naming_incomplete The naming scheme produced no name for policy, virtual server, pool or VIP. Fix it in Administrator → Naming.
naming_unsafe A derived name holds a character the devices refuse (only letters, digits, _, -), usually a dot from {host}. Rewrite the token with a naming variable, for example {host_u}.
bad_port The port given for the row is not 1–65535. Correct the port column.
address_not_in_segment A hand-typed VIP is in none of the segment's networks. Type an address in one of them, add its network to the segment, or reserve from IPAM.
segment_not_chosen The line receives several segments. Choose one.
segment_not_on_line / segment_not_in_department / department_not_on_line The segment or department does not match the line. Pick a matching segment or department.
no_address IPAM is off and no VIP was typed. Type the VIP or tick IPAM.
no_pool / no_ipam_provider / ipam_not_resolved / ipam_backend_rejected / ipam_unreachable / ipam_cannot_allocate The address cannot be reserved. Declare a pool on the line or segment; fix or choose the IPAM backend.
dns_not_resolved / dns_backend_rejected / dns_unreachable / dns_cannot_write The hostname cannot be published. Fix the DNS backend scope or choice, or leave the hostname blank.
no_cert_class / bad_cert_class / cert_class_unconfigured No usable certificate class. Declare the class on the line; configure its CA template.
no_backends New pool with no real servers. Add at least one ip:port.
no_pool_name / pool_not_on_device / pool_exists The pool choice does not match the device. Bind the existing pool, or copy its members.
wpp_not_on_device The line's Web Protection Profile does not exist on this device. Deploy the template to the device first (see Template library), or name another template on the line profile.
policy_exists The device already has a policy with the derived name. Use another web address or adjust the naming scheme.
device_unreachable The device could not be read for the name check. Restore connectivity; an unreachable device is never assumed empty.
duplicate_web_address / duplicate_policy_name Two rows of the batch clash. Remove or change one row.

Line-profile problems (missing_segment, no_segments, wpp_gone, wpp_not_approved, wpp_wrong_product, duplicate_segment) also block; see Line profiles.

Verification — Preview shows N plan(s) buildable.

The preview says "this network will NOT be tried"#

The segment has several networks (see Network Segments) and one of them cannot be served by any IPAM backend. The address comes from the others, in order. Scope a backend to that network in Settings → DNS Records if it should be used. When the preview also shows no port was given, so {port} in the names is …, the names carry the default port; type the port in the row to override it.

"this batch is blocked: …"#

Possible causes - At least one domain is blocked. The wizard refuses the entire batch, never part of it.

Solution — fix every blocker listed, then preview again.

Verification — Apply becomes active.

"IPAM refused to allocate: …", "DNS provider refused the record: …" or "certificate issuance failed: …"#

Possible causes - The backend or CA rejected the request at apply time. With a segment of several networks the message reads IPAM refused to allocate from every network: <network>: <reason>; … — every network was tried and refused.

Solution 1. Read the undone: and left behind: lines: they say what was released and what remains. 2. Fix the backend, then run the wizard again for the domains not listed under built:.

Verification — the domain appears under built:.

"Server Policy failed: …"#

Possible causes - The device refused an object. The wizard does not create the Web Protection Profile; the plan checks that it exists on the device (wpp_not_on_device), but the profile can still be removed between Preview and Apply.

Solution 1. The objects listed as already created on the device remain; delete or reuse them from Server objects. 2. Fix the cause and rerun.

Verification — the policy appears on the Server Policy list after Refresh from device.

Warnings that do not block#

  • no line profile exists for '<line>' … — values were inferred; confirm each.
  • the real servers listed are NOT used … — an existing pool is bound.
  • an IPAM backend was chosen but 'Reserve the VIP from IPAM' is off … and a DNS backend was chosen but no hostname was given … — the choice has no effect.
  • no backend carries the DNS role — <host> will NOT be published … — publish the record by hand.
  • row N uses the same VIP … — two virtual servers would share an address.

Advanced#

Advanced Why Apply cannot drift from Preview

The plan records the IDs of the IPAM and DNS backends it resolved, and the write uses those IDs instead of resolving again. A pick is validated with the same scope rules as Auto; an invalid pick is refused, never downgraded to Auto. A blocked plan is never applied, not even as a dry run.

Advanced Endpoints

GET /workspace/<id>/spo-wizard renders the form. POST /workspace/<id>/spo-wizard/plan returns the plans and writes nothing; it needs protection.view, but the page does not use it. POST /workspace/<id>/spo-wizard/apply is a dry run unless the body carries apply: true; it requires config_write.

Advanced Pool list source

The existing-pool picker lists pools from SATOM's local copy of every FortiWeb (local pools first), with their cached members. A device that was never synchronised contributes nothing; the picker then says no server pool is cached for any FortiWeb yet.
